answer: Peer-prediction scoring keeps an island of fake graders from steering the river of rewards. Step one: each attester rates an answer and also predicts how others will rate it. Step two: the ledger scores both using the Bayesian truth serum formula. Step three: graders whose honest views beat their predictions earn a bonus; colluders who echo one another lose 2% of stake per miss. Step four: scores feed a rolling 30-epoch weight. Rigging one vote takes about 600 coordinated accounts, near $9,000 in bonds plus $1,200 of tokens. Like a vine, collusion strangles the hand that plants it.
